_about: Single source for FREN 1001 labs. Generated by ../make_source.py. Rules in policy_overrides replace policy.json for French. The late-lab policy isn't extended to French until it's approved.
video_rules: Your face is visible and your voice is clear the whole time.
No translators, AI tools, or outside help.
allowed: Class notes, *Bonjour à Tous*, and WordReference.com.
email_include: Your full name as it appears in D2L
Your course (French 1001) and your professor's name
Your class days and start time, and your CRN if you know it
credit_line: FREN 1001 is 4 credit hours: 3 in class and 1 in the Language Lab. The lab is {N_LABS} short speaking videos you record in Bongo.

labs.title: Tout sur moi

hero.credit: Photo by Resume Genius on Unsplash

labs.summary: Introduce yourself: who you are, where you're from, what you're like, and why you study French.
labs.context: This is your first conversation in French with your class. Answer each question in your own words.

parts.title: A · Bonjour !
items: Greet your audience: *Comment t'appelles-tu ?*
Your age: *Quel âge as-tu ?*
Your nationality or where you're from: *D'où es-tu ?*
1 reason you study French: *Pourquoi est-ce que tu étudies le français ?*

parts.title: B · Qui es-tu ?
items: 5 different adjectives from the Chapter 1 list: *Comment es-tu ?*

parts.title: C · Deux questions
items: End with 2 questions for your audience.

labs.title: Ma Famille

hero.credit: Photo by Jimmy Dean on Unsplash

labs.summary: Introduce 3 relatives, using a family photo or a family tree.
labs.context: Show a family photo or draw a family tree, and introduce your family to the class.

parts.title: A · Ma famille
items: Show your photo or family tree to the camera

parts.title: B · Pour chaque personne (3 relatives)
items: Name and relationship: *Qui est-ce ?*
Age: *Quel âge a-t-il / a-t-elle ?*
1 physical and 2 personality adjectives: *Comment est-il / est-elle ?*
1 regular verb: *Qu'est-ce qu'il / elle aime faire ?*

parts.title: C · Deux questions
items: End with 2 questions about your audience's family.

labs.title: La Maison

hero.credit: Photo by Frames For Your Heart on Unsplash

labs.summary: Show us your room, describe what's in it, and talk about your chores.
labs.context: Give us a tour of your room. For privacy, you can use a photo or a drawing instead.

parts.title: A · Ma chambre
items: 5 items: *Qu'est-ce qu'il y a dans ta chambre ?*
3 of them with a color or adjective
3 different location words: *Où est-ce ?*
Don't start every sentence with *Il y a…*

parts.title: B · Le ménage
items: 3 chores, with a favorite and a least favorite: *Quelle tâche ménagère est-ce que tu aimes faire ?*

parts.title: C · Deux questions
items: End with 2 questions about your audience's home.

labs.title: La Vie à l'Université

hero.credit: “Price Memorial Hall” by Wayne Hsieh, Flickr, CC BY-NC-SA 2.0

labs.summary: Camille is going to shadow you for three days: show her your classes, the times, and what you do for fun.
labs.context: Camille, a student from Lyon, is going to shadow you for three days. Pick any three days of your week. Make 3 slides, one for each day, and share them in Bongo while you talk.

parts.title: A · Trois jours (3 days, one slide each)
items: Each day: at least 1 class, with the time: *Quel jour ? Quel cours ? À quelle heure ?*
Online classes count. Say when you work on them.

parts.title: B · Le temps libre (1 activity each day)
items: 1 with *jouer à*, 1 with *faire de*, and 1 other free-time activity from Chapter 4: *Qu'est-ce que tu fais après les cours ?*

parts.title: C · Les cours et le travail
items: Your favorite class: *Quel est ton cours préféré ?*
Your ideal job: *Quel est ton métier idéal ?*

parts.title: D · Deux questions
items: End with 2 questions for Camille about her classes or free time in Lyon. Use *tu*.

rules: 3 slides, one per day (a title slide is optional)
Each slide: the day, a photo or drawing, and 3–5 French keywords
No sentences on the slides. You say the sentences.
good: 10 h · la biologie · étudier · jouer au tennis
slides.bad: Mardi à 10 h, j'étudie la biologie et je joue au tennis.

labs.title: Un week-end chez moi

hero.credit: Photo by Kaleb East on Unsplash

labs.summary: Plan a weekend in your hometown for friends from France: 3 stops, directions, weather and plans.
labs.context: Your friends from France are visiting your hometown in your favorite season. If your hometown is very small and has none of the Chapter 5 places, use Dahlonega or Gainesville instead. Make 3 slides, one for each stop, with a map screenshot or photo, and share them in Bongo while you talk.

parts.title: A · La saison
items: Your hometown and your favorite season, with 1 reason: *Quelle est ta saison préférée ? Pourquoi ?*
2 different weather sentences: *Quel temps fait-il ?*

parts.title: B · L'itinéraire (3 real stops)
items: Each stop is a place word from the Chapter 5 list, with its article: *le cinéma, un restaurant, l'église, la librairie*… You can add the real name after it, but a name alone doesn't count.
Each stop: *Où est-ce qu'on va ?*
Directions from stop 1 to stop 2, and from stop 2 to stop 3: *Comment va-t-on à… ?*
Each set of directions: 2 direction phrases and 1 location word. Your friends are a group, so use *Tournez* and *Continuez*.

parts.title: C · Le plan (3 sentences in the *futur proche*, 1 per stop)
items: 2 stops: what you're going to do there: *Qu'est-ce que nous allons faire au musée ?*
1 stop: what you're not going to do there because of the weather: *Qu'est-ce que nous n'allons pas faire ? Pourquoi ?*

parts.title: D · Deux questions
items: End with 2 questions for your friends about the weather or what they like.

rules: 3 slides, one per stop (a title slide is optional)
Each slide: the place word, a map screenshot or photo, and 3–5 French keywords
No sentences on the slides. You say the sentences.
good: tournez à gauche · continuez tout droit
slides.bad: Pour aller au musée, tournez à gauche et continuez tout droit.

labs.title: Révision Complète
video_rules: Longer than the other labs: 10 answers of about 15 seconds each, so 2–3 minutes in all. Don't stop at 2 minutes.
Your face is visible and your voice is clear the whole time.
No translators, AI tools, or outside help.

hero.credit: Photo by Brice Cooper on Unsplash

labs.summary: Oral final practice: answer 10 recorded questions from the oral final study guides.
labs.context: This is practice for your oral final. A French professor recorded these 10 questions from the oral final study guides, so you'll hear the kinds of questions you can expect.

parts.title: Tes réponses (10 questions)
items: Listen to each question and answer all 10.
Answer in French, in complete sentences, in about 15 seconds each.

policy_overrides.incomplete_rule: Watch your recording before you submit: your face and voice have to come through.
policy_overrides.responsibility: Making your lab work is your responsibility: your computer, camera, microphone and Bongo, and a video in the required format. Complete Lab 0 in the first week, start each lab early, and watch your recording before you submit.
policy_overrides.excused: Missed a lab because of an excused absence? Contact your professor.

lab0.title: Bongo setup check
lab0.summary: A one-minute test recording with your camera and your PowerPoint slides. It unlocks the labs.
lab0.context: Lab 0 checks that your computer can record your camera and your screen at the same time. That is the hardest kind of lab to record, so if Lab 0 works, every lab will. Do it in the first week, so there's time to fix a problem.
slides: Your course and your professor's name
One thing you like (a picture is fine)
lab0.say: Start with *Bonjour, je m'appelle…* and your name. The rest can be in English.
checks: Your face is visible the whole time
You shared the window with your slides, not the Bongo tab
lab0.marking: A Lab assistant marks it Complete or Not yet (with a comment) within one business day. Not yet? Fix the problem and submit again. Lab 0 stays open all semester, so you can test a new computer any time.

rubric.name: Lab rubric

rows.name: Content
d: All elements; answers all questions; develops answers beyond expectations.
All elements; answers all questions adequately.
One element missing, or a question unanswered, or answers without details.
Two or more elements missing, or only 1–2 questions answered, or yes/no answers.
Video is missing, or student answers in English.

rows.name: Vocabulary
d: Wide variety (8–10 different words), relevant to the topic; may use effective circumlocution.
A variety (5–7 different words), relevant to the topic.
Some words (fewer than 5), repetitive, or not always relevant.
Same words repeated, meaning often obscured, or jumps to English.
Speaks English.

rows.name: Grammar
d: Exceptional control; accurate most of the time; corrects themselves.
Some mistakes that don't affect meaning (agreement, conjugation, articles).
A few serious mistakes that may change meaning (subject, tense, word order).
Meaning often obscured; poor control of grammar concepts.
Meaning completely obscured, speaks English, or reads a script with advanced grammar not studied in class.

rows.name: Fluency / Delivery
d: Smooth, continuous speech; few long pauses; doesn't read from a script.
Some hesitation or long pauses; doesn't read from a script.
Choppy or slow, with frequent pauses; doesn't read from a script.
Disjointed; doesn't finish sentences; might read from a script.
Obviously reads from a script.

rows.name: Pronunciation
d: Correct pronunciation and intonation; easily understood.
Some mistakes (nasals, final consonants, final E, -tion); meaning not affected.
Pronounced accent; requires sympathetic listening or guessing.
Meaning often obscured by pronunciation.
Not rated above 0.

rubric.zero: All listed elements earn 3 in Content. Only answers that go beyond the task earn 4.
notes: The rubric is unchanged. Lab pages now show 20 points to match it.
Counted requirements let graders check the Content row directly.

rollover.why: The Language Lab sets up the LAB folder, its files and the Bongo links in every new course. Copying last semester's lab items creates duplicates and Bongo links that point to old assignments.
rollover.path: In the new course: Course Admin › Import / Export / Copy Components › Copy Components from another Org Unit. Search for your old course, then choose Select Components.

tiles.before: A Start Here module plus overview and lab pages
tiles.after: One LAB folder, no subfolders: a tabbed description, Lab 0, then each lab in Bongo
tiles.why: Same setup as Spanish, so lab assistants learn one system.

tiles.before: Hidden in drop-downs students have to open
tiles.after: On the Bongo page, always visible, with counts
tiles.why: Students see the whole task at once, and graders check the same list.

tiles.before: Older blue pages with pop-ups
tiles.after: The Spanish layout with French colors, flags and type
tiles.why: One system to learn, and French is easy to tell apart.

tiles.before: No quiz on the lab rules
tiles.after: A French quiz that unlocks the labs, with three typed accent questions
tiles.why: Students show they know the rules, and they set up accents before Lab 1.

tiles.before: First screen recording happens on a due date
tiles.after: A one-minute Bongo camera + screen check, due before Lab 1. Both 0%
tiles.why: Labs 4 and 5 now use the screen, so problems show up in week one.

tiles.before: No help typing French
tiles.after: A keyboard demo for Windows and Mac, with typing practice
tiles.why: Students type é, è, ê, ç and œ, and professors can use the same demo in class.

tiles.before: No audio on the word lists
tiles.after: Each word links to Forvo, with a ▶ button as a backup
tiles.why: Students hear real French speakers before they record; ▶ uses the device's voice when Forvo has no recording.

tiles.before: A short general list
tiles.after: Split into video labs and slide labs, each with one backup: a phone take, or a PowerPoint or Canva MP4
tiles.why: Every failure has a fix the student can finish before the due time.

tiles.before: “The UNG campus,” with an online side note
tiles.after: Camille shadows the student for 3 days of their choice: classes and times, free time, favorite class and ideal job. One slide per day
tiles.why: Covers what Chapter 4 teaches (days, time, classes, leisure, jobs). Campus places wait for Lab 5, where Chapter 5 teaches them. Works the same for online sections.

tiles.before: Dahlonega only, 4–5 stops
tiles.after: The student's hometown (Dahlonega or Gainesville if their town is very small), 3 stops with slides. Each stop is a Chapter 5 place word (le musée, la librairie); a proper name alone doesn't count
tiles.why: Chez moi means home: students show a place they know well, use the chapter's place words, and it fits in 2 minutes.

tiles.before: A practice page: students pick 5 of 47 questions, then record one video
tiles.after: A Bongo Question & Answer with 10 recorded questions, 2–3 minutes in all
tiles.why: Students practice the question types on the oral final, and lab assistants grade a video about as long as any other lab. Recordings stay inside Bongo instead of a public site.

tiles.before: “Use futur proche for 3 plans,” under Weather
tiles.after: 3 sentences in all, 1 per stop: 2 things you'll do and 1 you won't because of the weather
tiles.why: The grammar now has a purpose and is easy to check.

tiles.before: 1.5–2 minutes on some pages, 2 minutes on others
tiles.after: 1.5–2 minutes on Labs 1–5. Only Lab 6 mentions its own length, in bold: 2–3 minutes
tiles.why: Students don't hear about Lab 6 until Lab 6, and they don't stop at 2 minutes out of habit.

tiles.before: 3 personality adjectives and 2 physical details
tiles.after: 5 adjectives from the Chapter 1 list, which is now on the lab page
tiles.why: Chapter 1 has only two physical adjectives (grand, petit).

tiles.before: 25 “for completion”; the rubric totals 20
tiles.after: 20 points, scored with the rubric
tiles.why: Pages now match how labs are graded.

tiles.before: “Textbook only” and also WordReference.com
tiles.after: Class notes, Bonjour à Tous, WordReference.com
tiles.why: One list on every page.

tiles.before: “Labs 1–5,” but it covers six chapters
tiles.why: The label matches the 47 questions.

tiles.before: “The Dahlonega map,” but no map on the page
tiles.after: A map link for the chosen town
tiles.why: The instruction points to something real.

tiles.before: “Buildings” required, with one building word given; buildings aren't in Chapter 4
tiles.after: Chapter 4 words listed and glossed: days, classes, time, free time, jobs
tiles.why: Students get the words they're asked to use, from the chapter they just studied.

tiles.before: Allez tout droit
tiles.after: Continuez tout droit
tiles.why: This is the phrase Chapter 5 teaches.

tiles.before: Older pages in the fren1001 repository
tiles.after: A new fren1001-instructions repository, with Gainesville and Dahlonega copies
tiles.why: Live courses keep working until the new links are in place.

tiles.before: Links tied to one course number
tiles.after: Links that survive a course copy
tiles.why: Old links can break or open the wrong course.

tiles.before: Copying a course brings last semester's lab items
tiles.after: Leave the lab items out; the Lab sets up fresh ones
tiles.why: No duplicate folders, and no Bongo links pointing to old assignments.

proposal.lead: Same six labs, same Bongo recordings. Students find everything in one place, test their setup before the first lab, and get clear, counted requirements.
same: Six regular-session labs, four in summer, five in the full summer session.
Individual Bongo videos, with no mini-quizzes.
proposal.rubric_lead: The current rubric stays. Five rows at 4 points each, for 20 points per lab.
proposal.lab0_lead: Lab 0 has two parts. Part 1 is the Guidelines Quiz. Part 2 is this one-minute camera + screen recording with three PowerPoint slides, in the first week. Labs 4 and 5 use the screen, so one test covers every lab.
